task: Rapid identification of high-fidelity internal battery parameters for an electrochemical-aging-thermal inspired digital twin using experimental discharge data and surrogate modeling.
named_method_commitments: Use an ANN meta-model or close neural-network surrogate to replace expensive physical simulations during parameter search.
Perform multi-parameter search over an LHS-style parameter space.
Produce identified internal parameters such as particle radius, reaction rates, and thermal coefficients.
Validate on constant-current discharge and assess generalization under dynamic conditions.

available_inputs: Experimental CC cycling data from CALCE CS2_36 Excel files
NASA PCoE aging discharge curves from MAT files
Oxford dynamic drive-cycle example from MAT file
missing_inputs: No direct ground-truth internal parameter labels
practical_workspace_interpretation.faithful_fallback: Construct a synthetic-but-physics-inspired low-order discharge/thermal simulator with interpretable internal parameters, generate Latin Hypercube samples, train ANN surrogates on simulator outputs, then identify parameters by minimizing mismatch to observed curves. Treat this as an MMGA-inspired surrogate identification study rather than exact reproduction of a full ECAT model.

primary_outputs_required: Identified parameter sets for representative constant-current reference cycles
Quantitative fit metrics between measured and fitted voltage/temperature/capacity curves
Dynamic-condition transfer evaluation on Oxford drive cycle
Traceable figures and tables supporting the claims
